233: def _branch_to_slug(branch_name: str) -> str:
234:     for prefix in ["fix/", "feature/", "bugfix/"]:

238:     return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9-]+', '-', branch_name.lower()).strip('-')[:60]

241: def _cleanup_merged_worktrees():
242:     """Delete worktrees and local branches for merged/closed bug-fixer PRs."""
243:     for state in ["merged", "closed"]:
244:         r = gh("pr", "list", "--repo", TARGET_REPO, "--state", state,
245:                "--label", "bug-fixer:system:pr", "--json", "number,headRefName",
246:                "--limit", "20")
247:         if r.returncode != 0:
248:             continue
249:         try:
250:             prs = json.loads(r.stdout)
251:         except json.JSONDecodeError:

254:         for pr in prs:
255:             branch = pr["headRefName"]
256:             wt_path = _find_worktree_for_branch(branch)
257: 
258:             if wt_path:
259:                 log(f"Cleaning up worktree for {state} PR #{pr['number']} (branch {branch})")
260:                 remove_worktree(wt_path)
261: 
262:             # Prune local branch (safe — PR is done)
263:             run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "branch", "-D", branch], check=False)

266: def _find_worktree_for_branch(branch_name: str):
267:     r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "list", "--porcelain"])
268:     current_wt = None
269:     for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
270:         if line.startswith("worktree "):
271:             current_wt = line.split(" ", 1)[1]
272:         elif line.startswith("branch "):
273:             ref = line.split(" ", 1)[1]
274:             if ref == f"refs/heads/{branch_name}":
275:                 path = Path(current_wt)
276:                 if str(path).startswith(str(WORKTREES_DIR)):
277:                     return path
278:     return None

280: def _branch_checked_out_at(branch_name: str) -> str | None:
281:     r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "list", "--porcelain"])
282:     current_wt = None
283:     for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
284:         if line.startswith("worktree "):
285:             current_wt = line.split(" ", 1)[1]
286:         elif line.startswith("branch "):
287:             ref = line.split(" ", 1)[1]
288:             if ref == f"refs/heads/{branch_name}":
289:                 return current_wt
290:     return None

292: def _remote_branch_exists(branch_name: str) -> bool:
293:     r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "ls-remote", "--heads", "origin", branch_name])
294:     return bool(r.stdout.strip())

296: def _fetch_branch(branch_name: str):

299: def ensure_worktree(branch_name: str, label: str = "") -> Path | None:
300:     existing_path = _find_worktree_for_branch(branch_name)
301:     if existing_path:
302:         run(["git", "-C", str(existing_path), "pull", "--ff-only", "origin", branch_name], check=False)
303:         log(f"Reusing existing worktree at {existing_path} for {branch_name}")
304:         return existing_path
305: 
306:     slug = label or _branch_to_slug(branch_name)
307:     wt_path = WORKTREES_DIR / slug
308:     wt_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
309: 
310:     if wt_path.exists():
311:         remove_worktree(wt_path)
312: 
313:     checked_out_at = _branch_checked_out_at(branch_name)
314: 
315:     if checked_out_at == str(REPO_DIR):
316:         log(f"WARNING: {branch_name} is checked out in main repo. Creating worktree from remote ref.")
317:         _fetch_branch(branch_name)
318:         r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(wt_path)])
319:         if r.returncode == 0:
320:             checkout_r = run(["git", "-C", str(wt_path), "reset", "--hard", f"origin/{branch_name}"])
321:             if checkout_r.returncode == 0:
322:                 return wt_path
323:             log(f"Failed to reset {branch_name} in detached worktree: {checkout_r.stderr}")
324:             return None
325:         log(f"Failed to create detached worktree: {r.stderr}")
326:         return None
327:     elif checked_out_at:
328:         log(f"Branch {branch_name} unexpectedly at {checked_out_at}. Returning that path.")
329:         return Path(checked_out_at)
330: 
331:     branch_exists_remote = _remote_branch_exists(branch_name)
332:     if branch_exists_remote:
333:         _fetch_branch(branch_name)
334:         r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", str(wt_path), branch_name])
335:     else:
336:         run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "fetch", "origin", "main"], check=False)
337:         r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", "-b", branch_name, str(wt_path), "origin/main"])
338: 
339:     if r.returncode == 0:
340:         return wt_path
341: 
342:     log(f"Failed to create worktree for {branch_name}: {r.stderr or r.stdout}")
343:     return None

345: def remove_worktree(wt_path: Path):
346:     if wt_path.exists():
347:         run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "remove", "-f", str(wt_path)], check=False)

465:             # --- Layer 1: Transcript-based liveness check ---

477:             # --- Check if PR was already opened (clean exit) ---

489:             # --- ORPHANED: transcript stale, no PR opened ---

492:             else:
493:                 log(f"Issue #{issue_num} — ORPHANED (conv {conv_id[:8]}... stale).")

495:             # Check for existing branch (durable code state)

498:             existing_branch = ""
499:             if r.stdout.strip():

502:             # Build reattach context

513:             if not reattach_lines:

517:             reattach_context = "\n".join(reattach_lines)

519:             branch_name = existing_branch if existing_branch else f"{BRANCH_PREFIX}/{issue_num}-reattach"
520:             wt_path = ensure_worktree(branch_name, label=f"issue-{issue_num}")

522:             if not wt_path:

525:                     log(f"CIRCUIT BREAKER: {branch_name} failed {count} times. Escalating.")
526:                     gh("issue", "edit", str(issue_num), "--repo", TARGET_REPO,
527:                        "--add-label", "bug-fixer:human:needs-intervention",
528:                        "--remove-label", "bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress")
529:                 log(f"Failed to create worktree for reattach #{issue_num}, skipping.")

531:             else:
532:                 _clear_failure(branch_name)
533: 
534:             prompt = (f"You are the bug-fixer agent. REATTACH to orphaned issue #{issue_num} in repository {TARGET_REPO}.\n\n"
535:                       f"Issue title: {issue_title}\n\n"
536:                       f"{reattach_context}\n\n"

538:                       f"Read config from: {CONFIG_FILE}\n"
539:                       f"Use safe_ingest.py at: {SAFE_INGEST} for all GitHub reads.\n"
540:                       f"Work in: {wt_path}\n\n"
541:                       f"The issue is already claimed (bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress label applied).\n"
542:                       f"Update the lock file at: {CLAIMS_DIR}/{issue_num}.lock with your conversation_id and PID.\n\n"
543:                       f"Continue from the best available state — DO NOT start over if there is existing progress.\n"

545:                       f"This conversation handles ONE issue only.") + CONTAINMENT.format(wt_path=wt_path, repo_dir=REPO_DIR, branch=branch_name)
546: 
547:             title = f"Fix #{issue_num}: {issue_title} (reattach)"

34: ## Core Concepts
35: 
36: An Antigravity **plugin** is a namespaced, shareable bundle that packages **skills**, **rules**, **hooks**, and optionally **MCP server configs** and **sidecar definitions** into a single deployable unit. Plugins are the recommended way to distribute complex agent behaviours.
37: 
38: A plugin has two distinct concerns:
39: 
40: | Concern | Where it lives | Mutable? | Committed? |
41: |---------|---------------|:--------:|:----------:|
42: | **Plugin code** (scripts, skills, rules, hooks templates) | `.agents/plugins/<name>/` | ❌ Immutable | ✅ Submodule |
43: | **Instance state** (config, claims, cooldown files) | `.agents/plugins/<name>-workspace/` | ✅ Mutable | Config: ✅ / State: ❌ |
44: 
45: The plugin directory is a **git submodule** (or standalone clone). It is treated as read-only after installation. All mutable state — configuration, runtime locks, circuit breaker files — lives in a separate **workspace directory** alongside it.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## Directory Layout
50: 
51: ### Standard Layout (Consumer Project)
52: 
53: ```
54: my-project/                                         ← REPO_DIR (derivable)
55: ├── .agents/
56: │   ├── plugins/
57: │   │   ├── bug-fixer-loop-plugin/                  ← PLUGIN_DIR (git submodule, immutable)
58: │   │   │   ├── plugin.json                         ← Manifest (required by Antigravity)
59: │   │   │   ├── hooks.json                          ← Hook templates with <plugin_dir> placeholders
60: │   │   │   ├── rules/
61: │   │   │   │   └── AGENTS.md                       ← Plugin rules (generic, not project-specific)
62: │   │   │   ├── scripts/
63: │   │   │   │   ├── install.sh
64: │   │   │   │   ├── uninstall.sh
65: │   │   │   │   ├── configure.sh
66: │   │   │   │   ├── engineering_dispatcher.py
67: │   │   │   │   ├── triage_dispatcher.py
68: │   │   │   │   ├── trajectory_dispatcher.py
69: │   │   │   │   ├── safe_ingest.py
70: │   │   │   │   └── pre_tool_gate.py
71: │   │   │   ├── skills/
72: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-engineering/SKILL.md
73: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-triage/SKILL.md
74: │   │   │   │   └── ...
75: │   │   │   ├── sidecars/                           ← Sidecar templates with placeholders
76: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-engineering-loop/sidecar.json
77: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-triage-loop/sidecar.json
78: │   │   │   │   ├── bug-fixer-pr-review-loop/sidecar.json
79: │   │   │   │   └── bug-fixer-trajectory-loop/sidecar.json
80: │   │   │   └── agents/
81: │   │   │       └── leak-auditor.md
82: │   │   │
83: │   │   └── bug-fixer-loop-workspace/               ← STATE_DIR (mutable, per-project)
84: │   │       ├── config.json                         ← Instance config (committed ✅)
85: │   │       ├── .gitignore                          ← Ignores runtime state only
86: │   │       ├── claims/                             ← Lock files (gitignored)
87: │   │       ├── cooldown.json                       ← Circuit breaker state (gitignored)
88: │   │       └── failure_count                       ← Consecutive failure counter (gitignored)
89: │   │
90: │   ├── hooks.json                                  ← Workspace-scoped hooks (resolved paths)
91: │   └── rules/
92: │       ├── bug-fixer-AGENTS.md                     ← Plugin rules (installed here)
93: │       └── 05-pio-lock.md                          ← Project-specific rules (human-authored)
94: │
95: ├── src/
96: ├── docs/
97: └── ...
98: ```
99: 
100: ### Key Principle: Path Derivation
101: 
102: Every path is derivable from the config file's own location:
103: 
104: ```
105: config.json is at:  <repo>/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json
106:                      │
107:                      ├── parent     = STATE_DIR  (.../bug-fixer-loop-workspace/)
108:                      ├── parent²    = plugins/
109:                      ├── parent³    = .agents/
110:                      └── parent⁴   = REPO_DIR
111:                      
112:                      STATE_DIR sibling = PLUGIN_DIR (.../bug-fixer-loop-plugin/)
113: ```
114: 
115: This means `repo_dir` and `plugin_dir` **never need to be stored in config**. Scripts derive them at runtime:
116: 
117: ```python
118: CONFIG_FILE = Path("...workspace/config.json").resolve()
119: STATE_DIR = CONFIG_FILE.parent
120: REPO_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent.parent.parent
121: PLUGIN_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent / "bug-fixer-loop-plugin"
122: ```
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## Discovery & Loading
127: 
128: Antigravity discovers plugins by traversing the `.agents/plugins/` directory tree. Each plugin directory must contain a `plugin.json` manifest:
129: 
130: ```json
131: {
132:   "name": "bug-fixer-loop"
133: }
134: ```
135: 
136: When discovered and enabled, Antigravity automatically ingests:
137: - **Skills** from `plugins/<name>/skills/` (progressive disclosure — name + description loaded, full content on activation)
138: - **Rules** from `plugins/<name>/rules/` (merged into active rule set)
139: - **Hooks** from `plugins/<name>/hooks.json` (registered for lifecycle events)
140: - **MCP servers** from `plugins/<name>/mcp_config.json` (launched and tools exposed)
141: 
142: ### Loading Priority (highest → lowest)
143: 
144: 1. **Workspace project** — `.agents/` walking up from CWD to repo root
145: 2. **Declared configs** — explicit `skills.json` or `plugins.json`
146: 3. **Global discovery** — `~/.gemini/config/`
147: 4. **Built-in customisations** — bundled with Antigravity
148: 5. **Global declared configs** — global JSON configs
149: 
150: Workspace-scoped customisations always win over global ones.
151: 
152: ### Enabling / Disabling
153: 
154: Plugin state is recorded in `~/.gemini/config/config.json`:
155: 
156: ```json
157: {
158:   "plugins": {
159:     "bug-fixer-loop-plugin": { "enabled": true }
160:   }
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: Toggle via CLI: `agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop` / `agy plugin disable bug-fixer-loop`.
165: 
166: ---
167: 
168: ## The Immutable Plugin Root Principle
169: 
170: > **The plugin directory is read-only after installation.**
171: 
172: This is the single most important architectural rule. The plugin directory (`bug-fixer-loop-plugin/`) is typically a git submodule. Nothing should write to it:
173: 
174: - ❌ No `config.json` with instance values
175: - ❌ No runtime state files (claims, locks, cooldowns)
176: - ❌ No `install.sh` writing back into it
177: - ❌ No sed/templating modifying files in-place
178: 
179: Scripts, skills, and agents are **used in-place** — never copied to global directories. The plugin root is the single source of truth for code.
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## Configuration Management
184: 
185: ### What Goes in `config.json`
186: 
187: The workspace config contains **project settings only** — no paths, no machine-specific values:
188: 
189: ```json
190: {
191:   "$schema": "bug-fixer-loop-config-v1",
192:   "target_repo": "owner/repo-name",
193:   "maintainer": "github-login",
194:   "trusted_users": [],
195:   "spec_file_path": "docs/design_specification.md",
196:   "protected_files": ["docs/design_specification.md"],
197:   "leak_patterns": ["ya29\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"],
198:   "max_concurrent_prs": 4,
199:   "test_command": "pio test -e native",
200:   "lint_command": "",
201:   "pr_prefix": "[BugFixer]",
202:   "branch_prefix": "fix",
203:   "triage_cron": "0 * * * *",
204:   "engineering_cron": "*/10 * * * *",
205:   "architect_cron": "*/15 * * * *",
206:   "trajectory_review_cron": "0 18 * * *",
207:   "triage_model": "flash",
208:   "engineering_model": "pro",
209:   "architect_model": "pro",
210:   "trajectory_model": "flash"
211: }
212: ```
213: 
214: This file is **committed to the consumer repo** — it documents the project's bug-fixer setup for the whole team.
215: 
216: ### What Gets Gitignored
217: 
218: Only runtime state is gitignored (via `.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/.gitignore`):
219: 
220: ```gitignore
221: claims/
222: cooldown.json
223: failure_count
224: triage_cooldown.json
225: triage_failure_count
226: ```
227: 
228: ### Config Discovery in Scripts
229: 
230: Scripts find the config through a standard search:
231: 
232: ```python
233: # Dispatchers (invoked from known location within plugin):
234: WORKSPACE_CONFIG = PLUGIN_DIR / "../../bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json"
235: 
236: # CLI tools (invoked from anywhere):
237: candidates = [
238:     plugin_dir.parent / "bug-fixer-loop-workspace" / "config.json",   # standard layout
239:     Path.cwd() / ".agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json",  # cwd fallback
240: ]
241: 
242: # Override via environment:
243: BUG_FIXER_CONFIG=/path/to/config.json python3 scripts/safe_ingest.py ...
244: ```
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: ## Hooks
249: 
250: Hooks are lifecycle interceptors that run external commands at specific points in the agent's execution. The plugin defines hooks in `hooks.json` with **placeholder paths**:
251: 
252: ```json
253: {
254:   "bug-fixer-file-gate": {
255:     "PreToolUse": [{
256:       "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content",
257:       "hooks": [{
258:         "type": "command",
259:         "command": "python3 <plugin_dir>/scripts/pre_tool_gate.py",
260:         "timeout": 10
261:       }]
262:     }]
263:   }
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: ### Path Resolution
268: 
269: The `<plugin_dir>` placeholder is resolved by `install.sh` at install time, producing a workspace-scoped `hooks.json` at `.agents/hooks.json`.
270: 
271: **Critical rule:** Hooks must be installed to the **workspace** `.agents/hooks.json`, never to the global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`. A broken global hook bricks every project on the machine.
272: 
273: ### Hook Working Directory
274: 
275: The hook command's working directory is set to the directory containing `hooks.json`. If hooks are installed at `.agents/hooks.json`, the cwd is `.agents/`.
276: 
277: ### PreToolUse Contract
278: 
279: The `pre_tool_gate.py` hook receives tool call details on stdin and returns a decision on stdout:
280: 
281: ```json
282: // stdin (from Antigravity)
283: {
284:   "toolCall": {"name": "write_to_file", "args": {"TargetFile": "/path/to/file.py"}},
285:   "conversationId": "...",
286:   "workspacePaths": ["/path/to/repo"]
287: }
288: 
289: // stdout (from hook script)
290: {"decision": "allow"}     // or "deny" with "reason"
291: ```
292: 
293: ---
294: 
295: ## Rules
296: 
297: Plugin rules live at `plugins/<name>/rules/AGENTS.md`. They are **generic** — applicable to any project using the plugin.
298: 
299: **Project-specific rules** (e.g., PlatformIO MCP lock protocol, framework-specific testing rules) belong in the consumer project's `.agents/rules/`, not in the plugin.
300: 
301: Example separation:
302: 
303: | Rule | Where | Why |
304: |------|-------|-----|
305: | "Never auto-merge PRs" | Plugin `rules/AGENTS.md` | Universal to all bug-fixer consumers |
306: | "Use PlatformIO MCP for builds" | Consumer `.agents/rules/05-pio-lock.md` | Only applies to PlatformIO projects |
307: | "Run `npm test` before PRs" | Consumer `.agents/rules/` | Only applies to Node.js projects |
308: 
309: The plugin's Step 9 (Verify) defers to project rules:
310: > *"Respect any project-level rules about build/test tooling. If the project rules mandate using MCP server tools instead of CLI commands, follow them."*
311: 
312: ---
313: 
314: ## Skills
315: 
316: Skills are multi-step agent procedures defined in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. They are **used in-place** from the plugin directory — never copied to global config.
317: 
318: Antigravity discovers skills via progressive disclosure:
319: 1. Only the skill's **name and description** (from YAML frontmatter) are loaded into context
320: 2. The **full content** is loaded only when the agent or user activates the skill
321: 
322: ### Skill Path References
323: 
324: Skills reference plugin scripts using `PLUGIN_DIR`, which is resolved at runtime:
325: 
326: ```markdown
327: ## Step 0: Configuration Guard
328: PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "<this_skill_file>")/../.." && pwd)"
329: STATE_DIR="<workspace_root>/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace"
330: ```
331: 
332: ---
333: 
334: ## Sidecars & Dispatchers
335: 
336: Sidecars are **background processes managed by Antigravity's runtime**. They are the mechanism for running recurring automated tasks — scheduled builds, periodic issue triage, cron-driven health checks — without requiring a user to be actively chatting.
337: 
338: ### How Antigravity Discovers Sidecars
339: 
340: Antigravity scans specific directories on startup for `sidecar.json` files:
341: 
342: ```
343: ~/.gemini/antigravity/sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json    ← Antigravity 2.0
344: ~/.gemini/jetski/sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json          ← Jetski / IDE
345: ```
346: 
347: > **These directories are inherently global.** There is no workspace-scoped sidecar discovery. This is the one place where the "nothing outside the plugin" rule can't fully apply — sidecars must be written to these runtime directories or Antigravity won't find them.
348: 
349: Each `<name>/` subdirectory represents one sidecar process. Antigravity reads the `sidecar.json` manifest and manages the process lifecycle.
350: 
351: ### Sidecar Manifest (`sidecar.json`)
352: 
353: A sidecar manifest defines what to run, how to schedule it, and what environment to provide:
354: 
355: ```json
356: {
357:   "builtin": "schedule",
358:   "args": ["*/10 * * * *", "/path/to/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py"],
359:   "restart_policy": "always",
360:   "display_name": "Bug Fixer Engineering (owner/repo)",
361:   "description": "Checks for eligible issues every 10 min.",
362:   "env": {
363:     "ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID": "project-uuid",
364:     "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:...",
365:     "BUG_FIXER_CONFIG": "/path/to/workspace/config.json"
366:   }
367: }
368: ```
369: 
370: | Field | Type | Description |
371: |-------|------|-------------|
372: | `builtin` | string | The sidecar type. `"schedule"` runs on a cron schedule. |
373: | `args` | array | For `schedule`: `[cron_expression, script_path]`. The script is invoked by the scheduler on each cron tick. |
374: | `restart_policy` | string | `"always"` restarts the sidecar if it crashes. |
375: | `display_name` | string | Human-readable name shown in the Antigravity UI/dashboard. |
376: | `description` | string | Shown in sidecar listings. |
377: | `env` | object | Environment variables injected into the process. **Critical** — see below. |
378: 
379: ### Sidecar Execution Model
380: 
381: When a `schedule` sidecar fires:
382: 
383: 1. **Antigravity's scheduler** wakes up at the cron interval
384: 2. **Forks a subprocess** running the script specified in `args[1]`
385: 3. The script runs as a **plain Python process** — it is NOT an LLM conversation
386: 4. The script's `stdout`/`stderr` go to Antigravity's sidecar logs
387: 5. The script is expected to **exit quickly** (seconds, not minutes)
388: 6. If the script needs to do LLM work, it spawns a **new conversation** via `agentapi new-conversation`
389: 7. The `restart_policy: "always"` means the scheduler continues firing on the next cron tick even if the script exits with an error
390: 
391: ### The `env` Block is Critical
392: 
393: **Sidecars do NOT inherit the user's shell environment.** The sidecar process gets a minimal environment from Antigravity's runtime. Without an explicit `env` block:
394: 
395: - **`PATH` is minimal** — `agentapi`, `python3`, `gh`, and other CLI tools won't be found
396: - **`ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` is unset** — `agentapi new-conversation` fails because it doesn't know which project to spawn into
397: - **`BUG_FIXER_CONFIG` is unset** — scripts can't find the workspace config
398: 
399: This was the root cause of a production failure: the sidecar templates shipped without `env`, so the installed sidecars pointed to scripts that couldn't find `agentapi` on the `PATH`. All 9 sidecar configs (3 sidecars × 3 directories) were silently failing on every cron tick.
400: 
401: #### Required `env` Variables
402: 
403: | Variable | Purpose | How to resolve |
404: |----------|---------|---------------|
405: | `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` | Identifies the project for `agentapi` conversation spawning | Detected at install time from `~/.gemini/config/projects/*.json` or from the active Antigravity context |
406: | `PATH` | Full `PATH` including `~/.gemini/antigravity/bin/` (for `agentapi`) and `/usr/local/bin` (for `python3`, `gh`) | Snapshot of `$PATH` at install time |

470: ### Dispatcher Architecture (The Non-LLM Control Plane)
471: 
472: Dispatchers are the Python scripts invoked by sidecars. They are **pure control plane logic** — they never call the LLM themselves. Their sole job is to decide whether there's work to do and, if so, spawn an LLM conversation to handle it.
473: 
474: #### Why This Matters
475: 
476: Running an LLM conversation costs money and burns quota. If the sidecar directly launched an LLM conversation on every cron tick, you'd spend tokens even when there's nothing to do. The dispatcher pattern keeps costs at zero when idle:
477: 
478: ```
479: Cron fires → Dispatcher runs  → No eligible issues → Exit immediately (cost: $0)
480: Cron fires → Dispatcher runs  → 2 eligible issues  → Spawn 2 conversations (cost: ~$0.50)
481: ```
482: 
483: #### Dispatcher Flow (Engineering — the most complex)
484: 
485: ```
486: 1.  Load config from workspace (WORKSPACE_CONFIG only — no plugin root fallback)
487: 2.  Derive REPO_DIR, STATE_DIR, PLUGIN_DIR from config file location
488: 3.  Check circuit breaker — if cooldown.json exists and not expired, exit immediately
489: 4.  Recover stale claims (3-layer detection):
490:     a. Claim file exists but has no conversation_id (spawn failed mid-write)
491:     b. Claim file older than TTL (conversation ran too long or was killed)
492:     c. Conversation exists but is in terminal state (idle/errored/cancelled)
493: 5.  Count active bug-fixer PRs via safe_ingest.py — if >= max_concurrent, exit
494: 6.  Query GitHub for eligible issues (via safe_ingest.py):
495:     - Has "bug-fixer:engineer:needs-fix" label
496:     - Not in exclusion_labels (e.g., "bug-fixer:human:required", "P1-blocker", "hardware-required")
497:     - Not already claimed (no active claim file)
498:     - Sorted by priority (milestone boost, label priority ranking)
499: 7.  For each eligible issue (up to max_concurrent - active_prs):
500:     a. Write claim file to STATE_DIR/claims/<issue_number>.json (atomic lock)
501:     b. Add "bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress" label to the GitHub issue
502:     c. Build the skill prompt (read SKILL.md, inject config values)
503:     d. Spawn LLM conversation via: agentapi new-conversation --model=<tier> --title=<title> <prompt>
504:     e. Capture conversation_id from agentapi stdout
505:     f. Update claim file with conversation_id
506:     g. If spawn fails: remove claim file, remove label, log error
507: 8.  Track spawn success/failure for circuit breaker
508: 9.  Log summary and exit
509: ```
510: 
511: #### Spawning Conversations via `agentapi`
512: 
513: The dispatchers use `agentapi new-conversation` to launch LLM sessions:
514: 
515: ```python
516: cmd = [
517:     "agentapi", "new-conversation",
518:     f"--model={model}",
519:     f"--title={title}",
520:     prompt,
521: ]
522: r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
523: ```
524: 
525: The `agentapi` tool is Antigravity's CLI for programmatic conversation management. It:
526: - Creates a new conversation in the Antigravity runtime
527: - Passes an explicit `--model` tier (`flash_lite`, `flash`, `pro`) based on role defaults or triage complexity labels, avoiding inheritance of arbitrary IDE defaults
528: - Injects the prompt containing instructions, paths, and issue/PR context
529: - Returns a JSON object with `conversationId` that can be used to monitor progress
530: - Requires `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` to know which project context to use
531: 
532: A successful spawn returns:
533: ```json
534: {"conversationId": "ec33ebf9-0cba-4100-8142-c61503f6c587"}
535: ```
536: 
537: A failed spawn (quota exhausted, missing env vars, etc.) returns a non-zero exit code and error text on stderr.

539: #### Stale Claim Recovery
540: 
541: The engineering dispatcher implements 3-layer stale claim detection to handle conversations that crash, timeout, or are killed:
542: 
543: ```python
544: # Layer 1: Claim file has no conversation ID (spawn failed mid-write)
545: if not claim_data.get("conversation_id"):
546:     recover(claim)
547: 
548: # Layer 2: Claim file older than TTL (conversation ran too long)
549: if claim_age > CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS:
550:     recover(claim)
551: 
552: # Layer 3: Conversation exists but is in terminal state
553: status = get_conversation_status(conversation_id)
554: if status in ("idle", "errored", "cancelled"):
555:     recover(claim)
556: ```

558: Recovery means:
559: 1. Remove the claim file from `STATE_DIR/claims/`
560: 2. Remove the `bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress` label from the GitHub issue
561: 3. The issue becomes eligible for the next engineering cycle

568:   "conversation_id": "ec33ebf9-0cba-4100-8142-c61503f6c587",
569:   "claimed_at": "2026-09-27T14:30:00+00:00",

576: ## Circuit Breakers
577: 
578: When the LLM quota runs out, dispatchers can enter a catastrophic failure loop:
579: 
580: 1. **Engineering loop fires** (every 10 minutes)
581: 2. **Finds eligible issues**, writes claim files, adds `bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress` labels
582: 3. **Spawns `agentapi new-conversation`** — all calls fail (quota exhausted)
583: 4. **Removes claim files**, removes labels (cleanup on failure)
584: 5. **Next cycle fires** — same issues are eligible again
585: 6. **Labels churn** on GitHub (added/removed every 10 minutes), user is spammed with dozens of failing conversation notifications
586: 7. **Repeat indefinitely** until quota is restored or the sidecar is manually stopped
587: 
588: ### Implementation
589: 
590: Each dispatcher tracks consecutive spawn failures using two files in the workspace state directory:
591: 
592: | File | Purpose | Format |
593: |------|---------|--------|
594: | `failure_count` | Number of consecutive cycles where all spawns failed | Plain text integer |
595: | `cooldown.json` | Present only when cooling down | JSON with `reason`, `entered_at`, `expires_at`, `expires_at_iso` |
596: 
597: #### Startup Check
598: 
599: ```python
600: COOLDOWN_FILE = STATE_DIR / "cooldown.json"
601: FAILURE_COUNT_FILE = STATE_DIR / "failure_count"
602: MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 3
603: COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 3600  # 1 hour
604: 
605: # Circuit breaker: check cooldown before doing any work
606: if COOLDOWN_FILE.exists():
607:     try:
608:         cooldown = json.loads(COOLDOWN_FILE.read_text())
609:         if time.time() < cooldown.get("expires_at", 0):
610:             log(f"ENGINEERING_EXIT: Cooling down until {cooldown['expires_at_iso']} — "
611:                 f"reason: {cooldown['reason']}")
612:             sys.exit(0)
613:         # Cooldown expired, clean up and resume normal operation
614:         COOLDOWN_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
615:         FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
616:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
617:         COOLDOWN_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
618: ```
619: 
620: #### Post-Spawn Tracking
621: 
622: ```python
623: # After the spawn loop completes:
624: if spawned == 0 and len(eligible) > 0:
625:     # Had work to do but couldn't spawn anything — this is a failure
626:     try:
627:         count = int(FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.read_text().strip()) + 1 \
628:             if FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.exists() else 1
629:     except (ValueError, OSError):
630:         count = 1
631:     STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
632:     FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.write_text(str(count))
633:     if count >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES:
634:         expires = time.time() + COOLDOWN_SECONDS
635:         COOLDOWN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps({
636:             "reason": f"{count} consecutive spawn failures",
637:             "entered_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
638:             "expires_at": expires,
639:             "expires_at_iso": datetime.fromtimestamp(expires, timezone.utc).isoformat(),
640:         }))
641:         log(f"Circuit breaker tripped after {count} consecutive failures. "
642:             f"Cooling down for {COOLDOWN_SECONDS}s.")
643: else:
644:     # At least one spawn succeeded, or no eligible work — reset counter
645:     FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
646: ```
647: 
648: #### Cooldown File Format
649: 
650: ```json
651: {
652:   "reason": "3 consecutive spawn failures",
653:   "entered_at": "2026-09-27T14:30:00+00:00",
654:   "expires_at": 1727447400.0,
655:   "expires_at_iso": "2026-09-27T15:30:00+00:00"
656: }
657: ```
658: 
659: #### Behaviour Summary
660: 
661: | Cycle # | Eligible Issues | Spawned | Failure Count | Action |
662: |:------:|:--------------:|:-------:|:-------------:|--------|
663: | 1 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 1 | Continue |
664: | 2 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 2 | Continue |
665: | 3 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 3 | **Trip breaker** — write `cooldown.json`, stop for 1 hour |
666: | 4–9 | — | — | — | Exit immediately (cooldown active) |
667: | 10 | 3 | 2 (quota restored) | 0 | Reset counter, normal operation resumes |
668: | 11 | 0 | 0 (no work) | 0 | No increment — counter only tracks "had work but couldn't do it" |

696: ## Anti-Patterns (Learned the Hard Way)
697: 
698: ### 1. Writing to Global Config
699: 
700: **Problem:** `install.sh` wrote hooks, rules, scripts, and skills to `~/.gemini/config/`. A broken global hook bricked every project on the machine. When an agent ran `git clean` and deleted the plugin directory, the global hook pointed to a missing script, blocking all tool execution across the entire installation.
701: 
702: **Fix:** Only write workspace-scoped artefacts. Scripts and skills are used in-place.
703: 
704: ### 2. Absolute Paths in Config
705: 
706: **Problem:** `config.json` contained `/Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/...` — completely non-portable. Can't be committed, can't be shared.
707: 
708: **Fix:** Derive paths from the config file's own location. The standardised directory layout makes every path computable at runtime.
709: 
710: ### 3. Instance Values in Plugin Root
711: 
712: **Problem:** `config.json` with `target_repo`, `repo_dir`, and `maintainer` lived in the plugin root. This meant:
713: - Dirty submodule after configuration
714: - Instance values committed to the plugin repo
715: - Only one project could use the plugin at a time
716: 
717: **Fix:** Config lives in the workspace directory (sibling of the plugin submodule). Plugin root contains no instance-specific files.
718: 
719: ### 4. No Circuit Breaker
720: 
721: **Problem:** When LLM quota ran out, the engineering dispatcher fired every 10 minutes, spawned conversations that all failed, churned issue labels on GitHub, and spammed the user with failing conversations.
722: 
723: **Fix:** Track consecutive spawn failures. After 3 failures, write a cooldown file and stop dispatching for 1 hour.
724: 
725: ### 5. Project-Specific Rules in Generic Plugin
726: 
727: **Problem:** Rule 16 ("PlatformIO MCP Lock Discipline") was in the plugin's `rules/AGENTS.md`. Every consumer — including Node.js, Rails, or plain Python projects — inherited a PlatformIO-specific rule.
728: 
729: **Fix:** Replace with a generic "Respect Project Testing Rules" rule. PlatformIO specifics go in the consumer's `.agents/rules/`.
730: 
731: ### 6. Copying Files Instead of Using In-Place
732: 
733: **Problem:** `install.sh` copied skills to `~/.gemini/config/skills/` AND `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/`, with `sed` templating to bake in absolute paths. This created 12+ duplicate skill directories that drifted out of sync with the source.
734: 
735: **Fix:** Skills are used directly from the plugin directory. Antigravity discovers them via the plugin's `plugin.json` manifest.
736: 
737: ### 7. Missing Sidecar `env` Block
738: 
739: **Problem:** Sidecar templates had no `env` field. The sidecar scheduler doesn't inherit the user's shell `PATH`, so `agentapi` couldn't be found.
740: 
741: **Fix:** Add explicit `env` block with `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID`, `PATH`, and `BUG_FIXER_CONFIG`.

# Issue #32: Autonomous-Mode Signal for Consumer Hook Differentiation

## Analysis Summary

After reading all four dispatchers, the hook mechanism, the sidecar configs, and the plugin architecture docs, the core question from the comments is valid: **the proposed env var won't reliably propagate across process boundaries.** The execution chain is:

```
Sidecar scheduler → Dispatcher process (Python)
    → agentapi new-conversation (subprocess)
        → Antigravity runtime creates conversation
            → Agent makes tool call
                → Antigravity fires PreToolUse hook
                    → python3 pre_tool_gate.py (hook subprocess)
```

Even if the dispatcher sets `BUG_FIXER_AUTONOMOUS=1` in its own `os.environ`, the `agentapi` call uses `subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)` which _does_ inherit the parent's env. But the agent conversation created by `agentapi` runs inside the **Antigravity runtime process**, not as a child of the dispatcher. The env var is lost at the `agentapi → Antigravity runtime` boundary.

---

## Recommended Approach: Conversation ID Registry

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The hook payload **already includes `conversationId`** (confirmed in [plugin-architecture.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/docs/plugin-architecture.md#L282-L289)). This makes a registry-based approach viable without upstream changes.

### How It Works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Sidecar as Sidecar Scheduler
    participant Disp as Dispatcher
    participant Registry as active_sessions.json
    participant AGY as Antigravity Runtime
    participant Hook as Consumer PreToolUse Hook

    Sidecar->>Disp: cron tick
    Disp->>AGY: agentapi new-conversation
    AGY-->>Disp: { conversationId: "abc-123" }
    Disp->>Registry: Register "abc-123" as autonomous
    Note over Registry: { "abc-123": { mode: "autonomous", ... } }
    
    AGY->>Hook: PreToolUse payload { conversationId: "abc-123", toolCall: {...} }
    Hook->>Registry: Is "abc-123" autonomous?
    Registry-->>Hook: Yes
    Hook-->>AGY: { decision: "deny", reason: "..." }
```

### Step 1: Dispatcher writes to registry

All dispatchers already capture `conversationId` from `agentapi new-conversation`. They already write it to dispatch tracking files in `STATE_DIR/dispatches/`. We extend this to maintain a consolidated registry:

**File:** `STATE_DIR/active_sessions.json`

```json
{
  "abc-123-def": {
    "mode": "autonomous",
    "dispatcher": "engineering",
    "issue_number": 42,
    "registered_at": "2026-10-03T09:43:14Z"
  },
  "xyz-789-ghi": {
    "mode": "autonomous", 
    "dispatcher": "architect",
    "pr_number": 15,
    "registered_at": "2026-10-03T09:50:12Z"
  }
}
```

### Step 2: Consumer hook scripts check the registry

Consumer projects (e.g., `esp32-app-foundation`) read the registry from their PreToolUse hook:

```python
# In consumer's pio-cli-gate.py hook
import json, os
from pathlib import Path

def is_autonomous_session(conversation_id: str) -> bool:
    """Check if this conversation was spawned by a bug-fixer dispatcher."""
    # Registry path is discoverable from BUG_FIXER_CONFIG
    config_path = os.environ.get("BUG_FIXER_CONFIG", "")
    if not config_path:
        return False
    registry = Path(config_path).parent / "active_sessions.json"
    if not registry.exists():
        return False
    try:
        sessions = json.loads(registry.read_text())
        return conversation_id in sessions
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
        return False

# In the hook's main logic:
payload = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
conv_id = payload.get("conversationId", "")

if is_autonomous_session(conv_id):
    # Autonomous mode — hard deny, no human to approve
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "deny", "reason": "Blocked in autonomous mode"}))
else:
    # Interactive mode — ask the human
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "force_ask"}))
```

### Step 3: Registry cleanup

The dispatchers already run `sweep_dispatches()` on each tick to clean up stale conversations. We add registry cleanup to the same sweep — remove entries whose conversations are no longer active.

### Step 4: Plugin provides a utility function

To avoid consumers reimplementing the check, the plugin exports a helper:

**New file:** [`scripts/session_mode.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/session_mode.py)

```python
"""Session mode detection for bug-fixer PreToolUse hooks.

Consumer hook scripts import this to distinguish autonomous vs interactive sessions.

Usage in consumer hooks:
    from session_mode import is_autonomous
    
    if is_autonomous(payload.get("conversationId", "")):
        return {"decision": "deny", "reason": "..."}
    else:
        return {"decision": "force_ask"}
"""

def is_autonomous(conversation_id: str, config_path: str | None = None) -> bool:
    ...
```

---

## Why This Approach Wins

| Criterion | Env Var | Marker File | Conv ID Registry |
|-----------|:-------:|:-----------:|:----------------:|
| Works for `run_command` hooks | ❌ Process boundary | ✅ Via `Cwd` | ✅ Via `conversationId` |
| Works for `call_mcp_tool` hooks | ❌ No `Cwd` | ❌ No `Cwd` | ✅ Via `conversationId` |
| Concurrent session isolation | ❌ Global state | ⚠️ Per-worktree | ✅ Per-conversation |
| No upstream Antigravity changes | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Survives conversation resumption (`send-message`) | ❌ Env lost | ✅ | ✅ Already registered |
| Clean API for consumers | ✅ Simple env check | ⚠️ Path gymnastics | ✅ Single function call |

> [!NOTE]
> The marker-file approach (option 2) is ruled out because `call_mcp_tool` hooks have no `Cwd` field — the exact gap described in the issue's "Workaround" section. The registry solves this completely.

---

## Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [`scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py) | Register conversation IDs after spawn (3 sites: fresh fix L867, reattach L569, PR iteration L731) |
| [`scripts/architect_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/architect_dispatcher.py) | Register conversation IDs after spawn (L342) |
| [`scripts/triage_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/triage_dispatcher.py) | Register conversation IDs after spawn (L169) |
| [`scripts/trajectory_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/trajectory_dispatcher.py) | Register conversation IDs after spawn (L203) |
| [`scripts/liveness.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/liveness.py) | Add registry management functions + cleanup in `sweep_dispatches()` |
| **New:** `scripts/session_mode.py` | Public API for consumers: `is_autonomous(conversation_id)` |
| [`docs/plugin-architecture.md`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/docs/plugin-architecture.md) | Document the autonomous session signal |
| [`README.md`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/README.md) | Document `session_mode.py` usage for consumers |

## Risk Assessment

**Low-Medium.** The change is additive:
- Dispatchers already capture `conversationId` — we just write it to one more place
- Hook payloads already include `conversationId` — no upstream dependency
- Registry is a JSON file in the existing `STATE_DIR` — no new infrastructure
- Consumer hooks opt-in to checking the registry — no breaking changes
- Cleanup piggybacks on existing `sweep_dispatches()` — no new cron jobs

The main risk is **stale entries** if cleanup doesn't run (e.g., sidecar stopped). Mitigation: entries include `registered_at` timestamps and the lookup function ignores entries older than a configurable TTL (default: 4 hours).

## Open Question

> [!WARNING]
> **Does `BUG_FIXER_CONFIG` propagate to consumer hook scripts?**
> 
> The hook scripts run as subprocesses of the Antigravity runtime, not of the dispatcher. If `BUG_FIXER_CONFIG` isn't in the hook's environment, the `session_mode.py` helper needs an alternative way to find the registry. Options:
> 1. Consumer hooks pass the registry path explicitly (from their own knowledge of the project layout)
> 2. The `is_autonomous()` function searches standard locations relative to the hook script's `cwd` (which is set to the directory containing `hooks.json`, per the architecture docs)
> 3. The registry path is passed as a hook argument in `hooks.json`
> 
> Option 2 is the most robust — the hook's cwd is `.agents/`, so the registry is at `./plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/active_sessions.json`, a known relative path.

96:             chunk = f.read(read_size).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
97:             lines = chunk.strip().split("\n")
98:             return json.loads(lines[-1])
99:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, IndexError):
100:         return None
101: 
102: 
103: def is_stalled(conv_id: str) -> bool:
104:     """A conversation is stalled if:
105:     1. Transcript mtime > STALE_THRESHOLD
106:     2. Last step is PLANNER_RESPONSE with no tool_calls
107:     (Agent emitted text and went idle — waiting for input that won't come)
108:     """
109:     age = transcript_age_seconds(conv_id)
110:     if age is None or age < STALE_THRESHOLD:
111:         return False
112: 
113:     step = read_last_transcript_step(conv_id)
114:     if step is None:
115:         return False
116: 
117:     return (
118:         step.get("type") == "PLANNER_RESPONSE"
119:         and not step.get("tool_calls")
120:     )
121: 
122: 
123: ERROR_LOOP_THRESHOLD = 3  # consecutive ERROR_MESSAGE steps to declare death spiral
124: 
125: 
126: def is_in_error_loop(conv_id: str) -> bool:
127:     """Detect conversations stuck in ERROR_MESSAGE death spirals.
128: 
129:     When an agent hits a terminal blocker (sandbox denial, forbidden command,
130:     file-not-found after compaction), it enters a state of consecutive empty
131:     ERROR_MESSAGE steps from which it cannot recover — even if a resume
132:     message is injected.
133:     """
134:     p = transcript_path(conv_id)
135:     if not p.exists():
136:         return False
137:     try:
138:         with open(p, "rb") as f:
139:             f.seek(0, 2)
140:             pos = f.tell()
141:             if pos == 0:
142:                 return False
143:             read_size = min(pos, 65536)
144:             f.seek(pos - read_size)
145:             chunk = f.read(read_size).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
146:             lines = chunk.strip().split("\n")
147:             # Count consecutive ERROR_MESSAGE steps from the end
148:             consecutive_errors = 0
149:             for line in reversed(lines):
150:                 try:
151:                     step = json.loads(line)
152:                 except json.JSONDecodeError:
153:                     break
154:                 if step.get("type") == "ERROR_MESSAGE":
155:                     consecutive_errors += 1
156:                 else:
157:                     break
158:             return consecutive_errors >= ERROR_LOOP_THRESHOLD
159:     except (OSError, IndexError):
160:         return False
161: 
162: 
163: # Blocker classification for recovery decisions
164: BLOCKER_STRUCTURAL = "structural"  # Will recur on retry — do NOT re-dispatch
165: BLOCKER_TRANSIENT = "transient"    # May succeed on retry
166: 
167: 
168: # Phrases in transcript content that indicate structural blockers
169: _STRUCTURAL_PHRASES = [
170:     "tool call denied by pre-tool hook",
171:     "user denied permission",
172:     "permission check failed",
173:     "Operation not permitted",
174: ]
175: 
176: 
177: def classify_blocker(conv_id: str) -> str:
178:     """Classify whether a stalled conversation's blocker is structural or transient.
179: 
180:     Structural blockers (forbidden commands, sandbox denials) will recur on
181:     every retry, so re-dispatching is wasteful. Transient blockers (plan-gate
182:     stalls, generic timeouts) may succeed on retry.
183:     """
184:     # ERROR_MESSAGE death spiral is always structural — the agent can't recover
185:     if is_in_error_loop(conv_id):
186:         return BLOCKER_STRUCTURAL
187: 
188:     p = transcript_path(conv_id)
189:     if not p.exists():
190:         return BLOCKER_TRANSIENT
191: 
192:     try:
193:         with open(p, "rb") as f:
194:             f.seek(0, 2)
195:             pos = f.tell()
196:             if pos == 0:
197:                 return BLOCKER_TRANSIENT
198:             # Read last 128KB for blocker signals
199:             read_size = min(pos, 131072)
200:             f.seek(pos - read_size)
201:             chunk = f.read(read_size).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
202: 
203:         # Check for structural blocker phrases in the tail of the transcript
204:         tail = chunk[-8000:]  # Last ~8KB is enough for recent steps
205:         for phrase in _STRUCTURAL_PHRASES:
206:             if phrase in tail:
207:                 return BLOCKER_STRUCTURAL
208: 
209:     except OSError:
210:         pass
211: 
212:     return BLOCKER_TRANSIENT
213:

219: def extract_context_from_transcript(conv_id: str) -> dict:
220:     """Read the transcript and extract a structured summary of what the agent
221:     accomplished before stalling.
222: 
223:     Returns:
224:         {
225:             "approach": str,
226:             "files_investigated": list[str],
227:             "blocker": str,
228:             "last_action": str,
229:             "artifacts": list[str],
230:         }
231:     """
232:     p = transcript_path(conv_id)
233:     result = {
234:         "approach": "",
235:         "files_investigated": [],
236:         "blocker": "",
237:         "last_action": "",
238:         "artifacts": [],
239:     }
240: 
241:     if not p.exists():
242:         result["blocker"] = "Transcript not found — conversation may have been cleaned up."
243:         return result
244: 
245:     try:
246:         with open(p) as f:
247:             steps = [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]
248:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
249:         result["blocker"] = "Failed to parse transcript."
250:         return result
251: 
252:     files_seen = set()
253:     artifact_paths = []
254:     last_model_content = ""
255:     last_tool_name = ""
256: 
257:     artifact_dir = str(BRAIN_DIR / conv_id)
258: 
259:     for step in steps:
260:         # Collect files from tool calls
261:         tool_calls = step.get("tool_calls") or []
262:         for tc in tool_calls:
263:             name = tc.get("name", "")
264:             args = tc.get("arguments", {}) if isinstance(tc.get("arguments"), dict) else {}
265: 
266:             if name == "view_file":
267:                 fp = args.get("AbsolutePath", "")
268:                 if fp:
269:                     files_seen.add(fp)
270: 
271:             elif name in ("write_to_file", "replace_file_content"):
272:                 fp = args.get("TargetFile", "")
273:                 if fp:
274:                     files_seen.add(fp)
275:                     if artifact_dir in fp:
276:                         artifact_paths.append(fp)
277: 
278:             elif name == "run_command":
279:                 cmd = args.get("CommandLine", "")
280:                 # Extract file paths from grep/find/cat commands
281:                 for match in re.findall(r'(?:/[\w./-]+)+', cmd):
282:                     if os.path.splitext(match)[1]:  # has extension
283:                         files_seen.add(match)
284: 
285:             last_tool_name = name
286: 
287:         # Collect model responses
288:         if step.get("type") == "PLANNER_RESPONSE" and step.get("content"):
289:             last_model_content = step["content"]
290: 
291:     # Extract approach from the longest model response (usually the plan)
292:     approach_candidates = []
293:     for step in steps:
294:         if step.get("type") == "PLANNER_RESPONSE" and step.get("content"):
295:             content = step["content"]
296:             if len(content) > 200:  # substantial responses
297:                 approach_candidates.append(content)
298: 
299:     if approach_candidates:
300:         # Use the longest substantial response as the approach summary
301:         longest = max(approach_candidates, key=len)
302:         # Truncate to first 1500 chars to keep the comment reasonable
303:         result["approach"] = longest[:1500]
304:         if len(longest) > 1500:
305:             result["approach"] += "\n\n_(truncated — see transcript for full context)_"
306: 
307:     # Filter files to only project files (not artifacts, not system files)
308:     result["files_investigated"] = sorted(
309:         f for f in files_seen
310:         if not f.startswith(str(BRAIN_DIR))
311:         and "/." not in f  # skip dotfiles/dirs
312:     )
313: 
314:     # Blocker is the last model response (usually ends with the stall question)
315:     if last_model_content:
316:         # Take last 500 chars — the blocker is at the end
317:         result["blocker"] = last_model_content[-500:]
318: 
319:     result["last_action"] = last_tool_name or "unknown"
320:     result["artifacts"] = artifact_paths
321: 
322:     return result
323:

341: def _format_state_dump(conv_id: str, context: dict, dispatch: dict) -> str:
342:     """Format a structured comment for posting to a GitHub issue or PR."""
343:     spawned = dispatch.get("spawned_at", "unknown")
344:     dtype = dispatch.get("type", "unknown")
345:     duration = ""
346:     try:
347:         spawned_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(spawned)
348:         elapsed = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - spawned_dt
349:         minutes = int(elapsed.total_seconds() / 60)
350:         duration = f" ({minutes} min)"
351:     except (ValueError, TypeError):
352:         pass
353: 
354:     lines = [
355:         f"[BUG-FIXER] ⚠️ Session stalled — context preserved",
356:         "",
357:         f"**Session:** `{conv_id}`  ",
358:         f"**Task:** {dtype.replace('_', ' ')}{duration}  ",
359:         f"**Last action:** `{context.get('last_action', 'unknown')}`",
360:         "",
361:     ]
362: 
363:     if context.get("approach"):
364:         lines += [
365:             "### What was accomplished",
366:             "",
367:             context["approach"],
368:             "",
369:         ]
370: 
371:     if context.get("files_investigated"):
372:         lines += ["### Files investigated", ""]
373:         for fp in context["files_investigated"][:20]:  # cap at 20
374:             lines.append(f"- `{fp}`")
375:         if len(context["files_investigated"]) > 20:
376:             lines.append(f"- _...and {len(context['files_investigated']) - 20} more_")
377:         lines.append("")
378: 
379:     if context.get("blocker"):
380:         lines += [
381:             "### Blocker",
382:             "",
383:             context["blocker"],
384:             "",
385:         ]
386: 
387:     if context.get("artifacts"):
388:         lines += ["### Artifacts", ""]
389:         for ap in context["artifacts"]:
390:             name = os.path.basename(ap)
391:             lines.append(f"- `{name}` → `{ap}`")
392:         lines.append("")
393: 
394:     lines += [
395:         "---",
396:         "_This context was automatically extracted from the stalled session's "
397:         "transcript. A human or the next bug-fixer cycle can continue from here._",
398:     ]
399: 
400:     return "\n".join(lines)
401:

447: MAX_ISSUE_DISPATCH_FAILURES = 2  # escalate after this many failures for same issue
448: 
449: 
450: def _issue_failures_path(state_dir: Path) -> Path:
451:     return state_dir / "issue_dispatch_failures.json"
452: 
453: 
454: def _load_issue_failures(state_dir: Path) -> dict:
455:     p = _issue_failures_path(state_dir)
456:     if p.exists():
457:         try:
458:             return json.loads(p.read_text())
459:         except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
460:             pass
461:     return {}

464: def _save_issue_failures(state_dir: Path, data: dict):
465:     _issue_failures_path(state_dir).write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2))

468: def _record_issue_dispatch_failure(state_dir: Path, issue_num: int,
469:                                     conv_id: str, blocker_type: str,
470:                                     log_fn=print) -> int:
471:     """Record a dispatch failure for an issue. Returns the new failure count."""
472:     failures = _load_issue_failures(state_dir)
473:     key = str(issue_num)
474:     entry = failures.get(key, {"count": 0, "history": []})
475:     entry["count"] = entry.get("count", 0) + 1
476:     entry["history"] = entry.get("history", [])
477:     entry["history"].append({
478:         "conversation_id": conv_id,
479:         "blocker_type": blocker_type,
480:         "failed_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
481:     })
482:     # Keep last 5 entries to avoid unbounded growth
483:     entry["history"] = entry["history"][-5:]
484:     failures[key] = entry
485:     _save_issue_failures(state_dir, failures)
486:     log_fn(f"Issue #{issue_num}: dispatch failure #{entry['count']} "
487:            f"(blocker={blocker_type}, conv={conv_id[:8]}...)")
488:     return entry["count"]

491: def should_skip_issue_dispatch(state_dir: Path, issue_num: int) -> tuple[bool, str]:
492:     """Check whether an issue should be skipped due to repeated dispatch failures.
493: 
494:     Returns (should_skip, reason).
495:     """
496:     failures = _load_issue_failures(state_dir)
497:     key = str(issue_num)
498:     entry = failures.get(key)
499:     if not entry:
500:         return False, ""
501: 
502:     count = entry.get("count", 0)
503:     if count < MAX_ISSUE_DISPATCH_FAILURES:
504:         return False, ""
505: 
506:     # Check if the most recent failures were structural
507:     history = entry.get("history", [])
508:     recent_structural = sum(
509:         1 for h in history[-MAX_ISSUE_DISPATCH_FAILURES:]
510:         if h.get("blocker_type") == BLOCKER_STRUCTURAL
511:     )
512: 
513:     if recent_structural > 0:
514:         return True, (f"Issue #{issue_num} has {count} dispatch failure(s), "
515:                       f"{recent_structural} structural — needs human intervention")
516: 
517:     # Even transient failures: skip after too many
518:     if count >= MAX_ISSUE_DISPATCH_FAILURES * 2:
519:         return True, (f"Issue #{issue_num} has {count} dispatch failures "
520:                       f"(all transient) — needs human intervention")
521: 
522:     return False, ""
523:

525: def clear_issue_dispatch_failure(state_dir: Path, issue_num: int):
526:     """Clear failure record for an issue (e.g. when it completes successfully)."""
527:     failures = _load_issue_failures(state_dir)
528:     key = str(issue_num)
529:     if key in failures:
530:         del failures[key]
531:         _save_issue_failures(state_dir, failures)

534: def _check_success(dispatch: dict, target_repo: str) -> bool:
535:     """Check whether the dispatched conversation achieved its goal."""
536:     dtype = dispatch["type"]
537:     spawned = dispatch.get("spawned_at", "")
538: 
539:     if dtype in ("fresh_fix", "reattach"):
540:         issue_num = dispatch.get("issue_number")
541:         if not issue_num:
542:             return False
543:         # Check if issue transitioned to awaiting-review
544:         r = _gh("issue", "view", str(issue_num), "--repo", target_repo,
545:                 "--json", "labels", "--jq",
546:                 '[.labels[].name] | any(. == "bug-fixer:architect:awaiting-review")')
547:         return r.stdout.strip() == "true"
548: 
549:     elif dtype == "pr_iteration":
550:         pr_num = dispatch.get("pr_number")
551:         if not pr_num:
552:             return False
553:         # Check if bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration label is gone (agent removed it after pushing)
554:         r = _gh("pr", "view", str(pr_num), "--repo", target_repo,
555:                 "--json", "labels", "--jq",
556:                 '[.labels[].name] | any(. == "bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration")')
557:         return r.stdout.strip() == "false"
558: 
559:     elif dtype == "architect_review":
560:         pr_num = dispatch.get("pr_number")
561:         if not pr_num:
562:             return False
563:         # Check for [ARCHITECT] comment posted after spawn
564:         r = _gh("pr", "view", str(pr_num), "--repo", target_repo,
565:                 "--comments", "--json", "comments")
566:         if r.returncode != 0:
567:             return False
568:         try:
569:             data = json.loads(r.stdout)
570:             for c in data.get("comments", []):
571:                 if "[ARCHITECT]" in c.get("body", ""):
572:                     # Good enough — architect posted something
573:                     return True
574:         except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
575:             pass
576:         return False
577: 
578:     return False

581: def _choose_resume_message(dispatch: dict, last_step: dict | None) -> str:
582:     """Select the appropriate resume message based on the stall signature."""
583:     blocker = ""
584:     if last_step and last_step.get("content"):
585:         blocker = last_step["content"][-300:].lower()
586: 
587:     # Detect plan-gate stalls
588:     plan_gate_phrases = [
589:         "shall i proceed",
590:         "would you like",
591:         "waiting for",
592:         "explicit approval",
593:         "plan gate",
594:         "shall i implement",
595:         "shall i go ahead",
596:         "do you want me to",
597:     ]
598:     if any(phrase in blocker for phrase in plan_gate_phrases):
599:         return RESUME_MSG_PLAN_GATE
600: 
601:     return RESUME_MSG_GENERIC
602:

604: def _recover(dispatch: dict, dispatches_dir: Path, target_repo: str,
605:              claims_dir: Path | None, log_fn) -> dict:
606:     """Execute the full recovery cascade for a stalled dispatch.
607: 
608:     Returns a summary dict for logging.
609:     """
610:     conv_id = dispatch["conversation_id"]
611:     dtype = dispatch["type"]
612:     dispatch_file = dispatches_dir / f"{conv_id}.json"
613: 
614:     # Classify the blocker before attempting recovery
615:     blocker_type = classify_blocker(conv_id)
616: 
617:     summary = {
618:         "conversation_id": conv_id,
619:         "type": dtype,
620:         "action": "unknown",
621:         "blocker_type": blocker_type,
622:     }
623: 
624:     # --- Step 1: Try to resume (skip if in error loop — resume is futile) ---
625:     error_loop = is_in_error_loop(conv_id)
626:     attempts = dispatch.get("resume_attempts", 0)
627: 
628:     if error_loop:
629:         log_fn(f"Conversation {conv_id[:8]}... is in ERROR_MESSAGE death spiral — "
630:                f"skipping resume (blocker={blocker_type}).")
631:     elif attempts < MAX_RESUME_ATTEMPTS:
632:         last_step = read_last_transcript_step(conv_id)
633:         message = _choose_resume_message(dispatch, last_step)
634: 
635:         if try_resume(conv_id, message, log_fn):
636:             # Update tracking — increment attempts, reset timeout
637:             dispatch["resume_attempts"] = attempts + 1
638:             dispatch["last_resume_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
639:             dispatch_file.write_text(json.dumps(dispatch, indent=2))
640:             summary["action"] = f"resumed (attempt {attempts + 1})"
641:             return summary
642: 
643:         log_fn(f"Resume failed for {conv_id[:8]}... (attempt {attempts + 1})")
644: 
645:     # --- Step 2: Extract context and post state dump ---
646:     context = extract_context_from_transcript(conv_id)
647: 
648:     if dtype in ("fresh_fix", "reattach"):
649:         issue_num = dispatch.get("issue_number")
650:         if issue_num:
651:             post_state_dump(target_repo, "issue", issue_num,
652:                             conv_id, context, dispatch, log_fn)
653:             # Clean up: unclaim the issue
654:             _gh("issue", "edit", str(issue_num), "--repo", target_repo,
655:                 "--remove-label", "bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress")
656:             # Delete lock file
657:             if claims_dir:
658:                 lock = claims_dir / f"{issue_num}.lock"
659:                 lock.unlink(missing_ok=True)
660:             wt_path = dispatch.get("worktree_path")
661:             if wt_path and Path(wt_path).exists():
662:                 _run(["git", "-C", str(Path(wt_path).parent.parent), "worktree", "remove", "-f", wt_path])
663: 
664:             # Record per-issue failure for re-dispatch prevention
665:             _record_issue_dispatch_failure(
666:                 dispatches_dir.parent, issue_num, conv_id, blocker_type, log_fn)
667: 
668:             summary["action"] = f"state dumped to issue #{issue_num}, unclaimed (blocker={blocker_type})"
669: 
670:     elif dtype == "pr_iteration":
671:         pr_num = dispatch.get("pr_number")
672:         if pr_num:
673:             post_state_dump(target_repo, "pr", pr_num,
674:                             conv_id, context, dispatch, log_fn)
675:             # bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration label stays — it was never removed
676:             # This means the next tick will re-dispatch (with the state dump
677:             # visible in the PR comments for context)
678:             summary["action"] = f"state dumped to PR #{pr_num}, bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration preserved"
679: 
680:     elif dtype == "architect_review":
681:         pr_num = dispatch.get("pr_number")
682:         if pr_num:
683:             post_state_dump(target_repo, "pr", pr_num,
684:                             conv_id, context, dispatch, log_fn)
685:             summary["action"] = f"state dumped to PR #{pr_num}"
686: 
687:     # Clean up tracking file
688:     dispatch_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
689:     return summary
690:

693: def check_orphaned_prs(target_repo: str, log_fn):
694:     """Warn on draft PRs matching the [BugFixer] Fix #N title convention that are missing system:pr."""
695:     r = _gh("pr", "list", "--repo", target_repo, "--state", "open", "--draft", "--json", "number,title,labels")
696:     if r.returncode != 0:
697:         return
698:     try:
699:         prs = json.loads(r.stdout)
700:     except json.JSONDecodeError:
701:         return
702:     for pr in prs:
703:         title = pr.get("title", "")

# Issue #32 — Revised Approach: Unified Local Session Registry

## You're Right: Conversation IDs Are Already Scattered Everywhere

After auditing the full codebase, here's the current inventory of conversation ID tracking:

| Store | Location | What it tracks | Lifecycle |
|-------|----------|---------------|-----------|
| **Claim lock files** | `STATE_DIR/claims/{issue}.lock` | `conversation_id`, issue number, worktree path | Created on claim → deleted on PR open or recovery |
| **Dispatch tracking files** | `STATE_DIR/dispatches/{conv_id}.json` | conv_id, type, issue/PR number, timeout, resume attempts | Created on spawn → deleted on success or recovery |
| **PR body HTML tags** | `<!-- agy_dev_conv_id: ... -->` in PR body | Developer conv_id for PR iteration resume | Persists in GitHub (non-local!) |
| **PR body HTML tags** | `<!-- agy_arch_conv_id: ... -->` in PR body | Architect conv_id for review resume | Persists in GitHub (non-local!) |
| **Issue dispatch failures** | `STATE_DIR/issue_dispatch_failures.json` | Historical conv_ids per issue, blocker classification | Grows until cleared on success |
| **Issue/PR labels** | GitHub labels (`in-progress`, `needs-iteration`, etc.) | State machine transitions | GitHub (non-local) |

### The Key Insight You're Raising

The **durable source of truth for state is GitHub** (labels, comments). But **conversation IDs are ephemeral and machine-local** — they're only meaningful to the Antigravity instance that created them. The PR body `<!-- agy_dev_conv_id: ... -->` tag is actually architecturally wrong in a multi-machine scenario — it bakes a local conversation ID into a portable GitHub artifact.

The dispatch files in `STATE_DIR/dispatches/` are already *de facto* a local session registry — they just don't expose a clean lookup-by-conversation-ID API, and they get deleted when conversations complete.

---

## Proposed Design: Extend Dispatch Tracking, Not Add a New Registry

Rather than creating a separate `active_sessions.json`, we should **consolidate and extend what already exists**. The dispatch files are the right primitive — they just need:

1. **A lookup function** that answers: "given a conversation ID, was this spawned by a bug-fixer dispatcher?"
2. **Retention of completed sessions** (currently deleted on success) — at least for the TTL needed by hooks

### Why Not a Separate Registry?

Adding `active_sessions.json` alongside `dispatches/*.json` and `claims/*.lock` creates a *third* local conversation tracking mechanism. You're right to push back on that — it's the opposite of parsimonious. The dispatch files already contain everything the hook needs.

---

## Exposure Mechanism: Hook Helper Script (Not MCP)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Decision: a simple Python helper script**, not an MCP tool.

### Why Not MCP?

| Criterion | MCP Tool | Hook Helper Script |
|-----------|:--------:|:-----------------:|
| Hook scripts can call it | ❌ MCP tools are for agents, not subprocesses | ✅ Direct Python import or subprocess |
| Works in `call_mcp_tool` PreToolUse hooks | ❌ Hook can't call MCP from inside a hook | ✅ Yes |
| Adds operational complexity | ❌ New MCP server to manage | ✅ Zero — it's a .py file |
| Consumer hook integration | ❌ Agent would need to query MCP first | ✅ `from session_mode import is_autonomous` |

MCP is the wrong abstraction level. The consumer is a **hook subprocess** (a Python script receiving JSON on stdin), not an agent. Hook scripts can't call MCP tools — they're not running in an agent conversation. They need a direct Python import or a file-system check.

### The Contract

The plugin exposes a single function that consumer hooks import:

```python
# Consumer's pio-cli-gate.py hook
from bug_fixer_session import is_autonomous_session

payload = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
conv_id = payload.get("conversationId", "")

if is_autonomous_session(conv_id):
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "deny", "reason": "PIO CLI blocked in autonomous mode"}))
else:
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "force_ask"}))
```

The implementation scans `STATE_DIR/dispatches/*.json` for a matching `conversation_id`.

### How Consumers Find the Dispatches Directory

The hook's working directory is `.agents/` (per [plugin-architecture.md L275](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/docs/plugin-architecture.md#L275)). From there:

```
.agents/                          ← hook cwd
  plugins/
    bug-fixer-loop-workspace/
      dispatches/                 ← scan this for conv_id matches
```

The helper script discovers this by walking from the hook's cwd — no environment variable needed:

```python
def _find_dispatches_dir() -> Path | None:
    """Discover dispatches dir from standard plugin layout."""
    # Hook cwd is .agents/ (set by Antigravity runtime)
    candidates = [
        Path.cwd() / "plugins" / "bug-fixer-loop-workspace" / "dispatches",
        # Fallback: check BUG_FIXER_CONFIG if set
    ]
    config_env = os.environ.get("BUG_FIXER_CONFIG")
    if config_env:
        candidates.insert(0, Path(config_env).parent / "dispatches")
    return next((c for c in candidates if c.is_dir()), None)
```

---

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Extend dispatch tracking (small change to [`liveness.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/liveness.py))

Currently `sweep_dispatches()` deletes dispatch files on success (L738). Change to:

- On success: move to `dispatches/completed/` with a TTL (e.g., 4 hours)
- On each sweep: purge completed entries older than TTL

This keeps the lookup function working for recently-completed sessions without unbounded growth.

Actually — **we don't even need this**. The hook only cares about *active* sessions. If a dispatch file exists, the session is autonomous. If it doesn't exist (completed/cleaned up), we don't know — but that's fine because the conversation is no longer doing anything. The hook fires during active tool use, which means the conversation is active, which means its dispatch file exists.

> [!TIP]
> **Simplification: just check `dispatches/*.json` for a matching conv_id. No retention change needed.** The dispatch file exists exactly for the lifetime the hook needs it.

### 2. New file: [`scripts/session_mode.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/session_mode.py)

~40 lines. Single function `is_autonomous_session(conversation_id: str) -> bool`.

- Scans `dispatches/*.json` files for matching `conversation_id`
- Discovers dispatches dir from cwd or `BUG_FIXER_CONFIG`
- Returns `False` if directory not found (safe default = interactive)
- Cached per-process (hook scripts are short-lived, but no point reading N files twice)

### 3. No dispatcher changes required

The dispatchers already call `record_dispatch()` with the conversation ID. The data is already there. Zero changes to [`engineering_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py), [`architect_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/architect_dispatcher.py), [`triage_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/triage_dispatcher.py), or [`trajectory_dispatcher.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/trajectory_dispatcher.py).

### 4. Documentation

- Add `session_mode.py` usage to [README.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/README.md)
- Add section to [plugin-architecture.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/docs/plugin-architecture.md) explaining the autonomous session contract

---

## Scope Boundary: What This Issue Does NOT Address

You raised the question of whether to revisit the broader conversation-ID-to-issue/PR mapping architecture. That's a separate concern:

| Concern | This issue (#32) | Broader refactor (separate issue?) |
|---------|:-:|:-:|
| "Is this conversation autonomous?" | ✅ | — |
| Consolidate claims + dispatches + PR tags | — | ✅ |
| Remove non-portable conv IDs from GitHub PR bodies | — | ✅ |
| Single local registry for all conv→issue/PR mappings | — | ✅ |
| Clean up the 5+ places conv IDs are tracked | — | ✅ |

> [!NOTE]
> The broader refactor is worth doing but is a separate piece of work. The `<!-- agy_dev_conv_id: ... -->` PR body tags are arguably wrong (non-portable), and the claims/dispatches/failures trio could be unified. But #32 can be solved cleanly without touching any of that — the dispatch files already contain everything needed.

---

## Summary

| Aspect | Decision | Rationale |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| **Registry mechanism** | Reuse existing `dispatches/*.json` | Already tracks all autonomous sessions — no new state file |
| **Exposure mechanism** | Python helper script, not MCP | Hook subprocesses can't call MCP tools |
| **New file** | `scripts/session_mode.py` (~40 lines) | Single function: `is_autonomous_session(conv_id)` |
| **Dispatcher changes** | None | `record_dispatch()` already creates the data |
| **Discovery** | Relative path from hook cwd (`.agents/`) | No env var dependency for the consumer |
| **Broader conv ID refactor** | Out of scope — separate issue | Keep #32 focused |

**Total implementation: ~40 lines of new code + docs. Zero changes to existing dispatchers or liveness.**
args.Description: Revised approach for issue #32 that reuses existing dispatch tracking instead of adding a new registry, exposes via hook helper script not MCP, and scopes out the broader conv-ID architecture refactor.
